text: We tested aggressive gradient clipping (clip_norm 0.1) during student fine-tuning in a weak-to-strong generalization setup, with gpt2-medium as the weak supervisor and mistral-7b as the strong student. The weak supervisor reached 0.64 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.89; the student trained on weak labels reached a transfer accuracy of 0.74 with a standard error of 0.03. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.41 with a standard error of 0.12, against a baseline PGR of 0.17. Importantly, this run used only num_seeds = 2, so the uncertainty estimates are themselves poorly constrained, and the margin between the measured PGR and the baseline does not exceed two standard errors of the PGR estimate. The direction of the effect is favorable, but on this evidence we cannot characterize gradient clipping as an improvement over the baseline; more seeds are needed before any such claim.
